selected_evidence.summary: node2 pinged node3 successfully (violating isolation) while node1's eth0 initially had no working address; later confirmed eth0 is the correct interface with working connectivity to both node2 and node3

selected_evidence.requirement: node2/node3 mutual isolation implemented and verified
selected_evidence.summary: iptables DROP rules added on node2 (blocking 10.100.147.12) and node3 (blocking 10.100.147.11); ping tests show 'Operation not permitted' between node2 and node3

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 both still reach node1 after isolation
selected_evidence.summary: node2->node1 and node3->node1 pings succeed (0% loss) while gateway reachability also confirmed
iptables-openrc enabled and rules saved to /etc/iptables/rules-save on node2/node3; rc-service iptables restart reloads identical DROP rules from disk
Captured node2 boot_id (547e44e4...), uptime, and firewall rules prior to restart

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: reboot command caused stream disconnect (acknowledgement); subsequent poll shows new boot_id f3f80661... and uptime 16.74s, proving an actual reboot occurred
After reboot, node2 iptables DROP rules present, ping to node1 succeeds, ping to node3 blocked with 'Operation not permitted'
Captured node3 boot_id (c331951f...), uptime, and firewall rules prior to restart

selected_evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: reboot command caused stream disconnect; subsequent poll shows new boot_id dae2038e... and uptime 20.41s, proving an actual reboot occurred
After reboot, node3 iptables DROP rules present, ping to node1 succeeds, ping to node2 blocked with 'Operation not permitted'
Captured node1 boot_id (34192023...), uptime, eth0 address, and successful pings to node2 and node3 prior to restart

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: systemctl reboot caused connection reset (acknowledgement); subsequent poll shows new boot_id 1b86c994... and uptime 10.38s, proving an actual reboot occurred (initial backgrounded 'reboot' attempt did not trigger a real reboot, confirmed by unchanged boot_id in cmd-5a8ada5839964bc0, so systemctl reboot was used instead)
After reboot, node1 eth0 re-acquired 10.100.147.10 via DHCP and successfully pinged both node2 and node3

selected_evidence.requirement: Final full-cluster verification: isolation and connectivity both intact after all three restarts
